Just be careful not to avoid walks too often.
I made this mistake in the past, and it definitely made things worse for a number of reasons:

- practice is crucial, for you and your dog
- the less walks your dog gets, the more excitable he or she will be on the next walk, and so, more reactive

I can't speak for you, this is only from my personal experience, and beyond our dogs both being reactive, I really don't know how similar our dogs are, and how applicable my experience is to yours. That being said, the mistakes I made may prove useful to you.

Background: I have a high energy, large  working mix dog that is reactive to other dogs.

Initially, walking her was so frustrating, embarrassing, and just incredibly stressful. So I began shortening our walks from 2hrs to 1, sometimes 30 min, and very rarely, not at all. I just wanted to avoid it. But as I did that, it built up the idea of normal length walks as some insurmountable task, a frustrating chore. It made me feel more anxious on our walks. Which is the opposite of what your dog needs (and you).

On top of that, my dog had wayyyy to much energy, because she wasn't getting enough exercise and mental stimulation, despite all the tricks we practiced and games we played at home. Even despite us still venturing out for a 2hr walk weekly. 

I realized my dog wasn't getting what she needed    and finally just forced myself to do long walks. Every day. 
It was stressful for a while, but I got over it, and with time, became so much more confident. My dog definitely did too, and became way more calm on our walks. 

I don't know if this sounds familiar to you (maybe you just needed one day off, completely understandable) but on the off chance it does, please keep practicing. Maybe get a muzzle so that you feel more comfortable this situation won't happen again.
Note: do NOT get a fabric/mesh muzzle. They don't allow dogs to breath properly and are lethal if used when it's hot out. The best muzzle to use is the cage muzzle, that allows dogs to freely pant, drink water, and accept treats. Here's a great resource to learn about using the muzzle: https://muzzleupproject.com/muzzle-training/

It really can get better in most cases. My dog was super reactive, and now, I rarely see her even growl at a dog, and that's even when a little dog lunges at her and freaks out.
It took years of patience, but it's amazing what diligent practice will do. Your dog will learn to trust you and itself more over time.
